pure-announcement.rationale: It is the full text of an IETF Standards Track specification, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: No listed neighbour concerns JOSE, key types, or modern-curve cryptography; the MCP and skills concepts are a different subject entirely.

unfalsifiable.rationale: It is a normative primary source whose signing, verification, and ECDH procedures include worked test vectors any implementer can reproduce.

durability.rationale: The OKP key type and EdDSA/X25519/X448 JOSE bindings have been stable IETF standards since 2017 and remain the authoritative way to use modern curves in JWS/JWE, so the content will hold in twelve months.

actionability.rationale: It prescribes the exact key representation, signing and verification procedures, and registry values an implementer builds against, plus concrete security rules such as never separating key material from its subtype to avoid algorithm-confusion attacks.

atomicity.rationale: The document carries one idea — how the CFRG curves are used in JOSE via the OKP key type — and every section, registry entry, and example serves it.
